title: TotalEnergies subsidiary Saft manufactures solid-state batteries in Bordeaux - electrive.com
content:
Battery manufacturer Saft, part of the TotalEnergies group, is inaugurating new production lines for solid-state batteries at its Bordeaux facility. The batteries are primarily intended for use in aerospace applications. Saft does not mention any potential use in road vehicles.
Image: Saft
Saft describes itself as the first French manufacturer to produce self-developed solid-state batteries that utilise both sulphide and polymer electrolytes at room temperature. The Total subsidiary cites aerospace as a key application area, where “gains in safety, performance and energy density are particularly valuable,” according to an accompanying statement. In aviation, Saft has already
made a strong initial impact
with the recent delivery of semi-solid-state cells in collaboration with partner Safran.
According to Saft, the new production lines in Bordeaux – a European aerospace hub – are designed to accommodate various technologies, specifically both polymer-based semi-solid-state batteries and sulphide-based solid-state batteries. The facilities operate explicitly at room temperature. However, Saft remains vague about the batteries themselves, stating only that they will be particularly safe and compact. Their energy density is said to be up to 50 per cent higher than that of conventional lithium-ion batteries. Additionally, the manufacturing process uses a dry electrode method, which is expected to reduce CO₂ emissions in production by up to 40 per cent.
Saft CEO Cédric Duclos commented: “Solid-state batteries are among the most promising innovations for meeting tomorrow’s electrification needs. These new production lines mark an important milestone for Saft, as we turn several years of research into real industrial capacity, a statement of our ambition to establish France and Europe as leading players in this strategic technology.”
France also has another producer of already commercialised solid-state batteries in Blue Solutions, part of the Bolloré conglomerate. In this case, the technology is based on lithium-metal-polymer (LMP). However,
Blue Solutions is currently being restructured
after issues arose with the batteries in serial applications, particularly in buses.
Saft is best known to us as a shareholder in the joint venture
Automotive Cells Company (ACC)
. The manufacturer is owned by Saft, Stellantis and Mercedes-Benz and produces nickel-based cells and modules in France, which currently primarily benefit Stellantis. The Douvrin site was originally supposed to be supplemented by two additional plants in Germany and Italy. However, the joint venture is now focusing solely on the ramp-up phase at its only cell factory in France. The other two major projects
have been scrapped
Beyond this, Saft has repeatedly stood out for its research efforts. For example, together with Stellantis and other partners, the Total subsidiary is working on
a battery with integrated inverter and charging functions
. In the European research project
, Saft also focused on sulphide-based solid-state batteries in collaboration with other players starting in 2023. In the
TALISSMAN
project, Saft is working with partners to develop lithium-sulphur batteries for electric vehicles.

title: Maersk Singapore Ethanol Bunkering Sets Technical Milestone
content:
Maersk Singapore Ethanol Bunkering Sets Technical Milestone
Prioritise Us
on Google
Maersk, the Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore and a local supplier conducted a bunkering operation of a 5,000t stem of ethanol on 17 October 2026. Credit: MPA
Emma Mazhari, Head of Energy Markets at Maersk, explains how a 5,000-tonne Singapore bunkering operation supports the company’s multi-fuel strategy
Maersk completed an ethanol bunkering operation at the Port of Singapore on 18 October 2026.
The bunkering operation saw a 5,000 tonne stem of bioethanol bunkered aboard Maersk’s container vessel Maersk Halifax at the Pasir Panjang terminal at the Port of Singapore.
The operation represented a number of firsts: it was the first ethanol bunkering operation to be concluded at the Pasir Panjang terminal, and the first ethanol bunkering operation for a vessel retrofitted to ethanol operation for Maersk. The 5,000t stem of ethanol was also the largest volume of ethanol to be bunkered globally to date.
The 5,000t of ISCC-certified bioethanol was supplied via a mass flow meter while container operations were conducted simultaneously (SIMOPS). The Maritime and Port Authority of Singapore noted that the operation was intended to provide useful operational experience of handling ethanol, as well as to demonstrate whether existing MFM infrastructure was compatible with ethanol bunkering.
The MPA also noted that the operation will provide data and learning points which will be taken into account when Singapore’s port authorities examines how its existing methanol bunkering standards (or technical reference 129) could be adapted for ethanol bunkering.
The bunkering operation was conducted by a local Singaporean bunker supply operator, Golden Island. The stem was delivered by a chemical tanker, M.T. Golden Centaurus.
Maersk’s ethanol focus
Ethanol is emerging as a promising transition fuel because of its global availability, established production and distribution networks, and compatibility with alcohol-enabled engine technologies. When certified and sourced from low-carbon pathways, ethanol can deliver significant greenhouse gas reductions compared with conventional marine fuels.
“The energy transition requires us to explore and scale solutions that can deliver real-world impact,” Emma Mazhari, Head of Energy Markets, Maersk.
“At Maersk, we continue to pursue a multi-fuel strategy because we recognise that no single fuel pathway can decarbonise global shipping on its own.”
Earlier this year, Maersk conducted a series of successful ethanol trials on the dual-fuel vessels Laura Maersk, Antonia Maersk and Tangier Maersk.
Maersk completed the first ship-to-ship commercial ethanol bunkering of a deep-sea container vessel in the US at the Port of Mobil in late September 2026. Credit: Alabama Port Authority
Growing interest in ethanol as a bunker fuel
While the bunkering operation was timed to coincide with a trade event focused on bunkering, SIBCON, Singapore is also seeking to update its domestic regulations to handle ethanol fuelled vessels.
In October, Brazil-based mining major Vale announced that it was entering into a long term charter agreement for two 210,000 deadweight tonne (DWT) vessels from MOL Ocean Bulk. The two vessels will be capable of operating fuel oil, methanol and ethanol when they are delivered in 2030.
“Designing and constructing new ships is the most cost-effective and integrated opportunity to incorporate technological advances in our decarbonisation program,” says Rodrigo Bermelho, Shipping Director at Vale. “This approach provides flexibility during regulatory and market uncertainty, enabling Vale to advance decarbonisation whilst maintaining different strategic options.”
Earlier in the year, Vale
announced
that it was chartering a pair of 325,000 DWT dual fuel dry bulk carriers capable of operating on ethanol from Chinese ship operator Shandong Shipping. The vessels will be the first deep-sea vessels capable of operating on ethanol when they enter service in 2029.
The order was announced alongside a larger order for 10 325,000 DWT ore carriers. Shipping analysts from London based analysts Drewry
that the order represented a return to ship ownership for Vale and was consistent with Vale’s logistics strategy to reduce shipping costs by ordering larger more efficient ore carriers to compete against iron ore majors BHP and Rio Tinto. BHP and Rio benefit from much shorter supply chains between Western Australia and their largest markets in China and elsewhere in East Asia.
Vale and Mitsui O.S.K. Lines' subsidiary, MOL Ocean Bulk, agreed a 25-year contract to transport iron ore using two tri-fuel (ethanol, methanol and fuel oil) powered dry bulk carriers on 2 October 2026. Credit: MOL Ocean Bulk
Ethanol and methanol as shipping fuels
Ethanol is well established as a transportation fuel in some countries in the world. According to Brazil's Energy Research Office (EPE), ethanol production in Brazil is currently around 35.7 billion litres.
The fuel shares several characteristics with methanol, creating opportunities to leverage existing investments in methanol-fuelled engines, bunkering infrastructure and technical experience, leading classification society DNV notes.
However, the classification society cautions that the adoption of alternative fuels in the shipping market is influenced by practical concerns, such as whether ethanol can compete economically, and whether the infrastructure exists for the fuel to be supplied at scale.
Key facts about Maersk Halifax ethanol bunkering
Fuel: Approximately 5,000 metric tonnes of ISCC-certified bioethanol were bunkered.
Vessel: Singapore-registered Maersk Halifax received the fuel.
Location: The operation took place at PSA’s Pasir Panjang Terminal.
Supplier: Golden Island supplied the fuel from M.T. Golden Centaurus.
Measurement: A mass flow meter measured the transferred fuel.
Operations: Bunkering took place simultaneously with container operations.
Regulation: MPA is assessing whether Technical Reference 129 can be adapted for ethanol.
Emissions: Lifecycle reductions depend on the ethanol feedstock and production pathway.

A-P Moller Maersk is an integrated logistics company. Maersk operates four business segments: Ocean, Logistics and Services, Terminals and Towage, and Manufacturing and Others. As a global leader in shipping services, the company operates in more than 130 countries and employs over 100,000 people worldwide. Maersk is aiming to reach net zero emissions by 2040 across the entire business with new technologies, new vessels, and green fuels.

Vale is one of the world’s largest mining companies, with operations in a range of metals and minerals. Headquartered in Brazil and operating around the world, it is one of the world's leading producers of iron ore, copper and nickel. Its operations comprise extensive logistics systems integrated with its mines, including railroads, maritime terminals, and ports. Since 2020, Vale has invested around US$ 1.4 billion to reduce its Scope 1, 2 and 3 emissions. The company has committed to reducing Scope 3 emissions by 15% by 2035, relating to the value chain, which includes the majority of emissions from maritime transport, depending on the type of contract.

title: Surgere: Why Agentic AI Requires Strong Supply Chain Data
content:
Surgere: Why Agentic AI Requires Strong Supply Chain Data
Prioritise Us
on Google
Surgere argues that agentic AI Is only as good as the supply chain data beneath it. Credit: Getty Images
As organisations implement AI into their supply chain operations, Surgere is driving home the importance of data accuracy, CEO William Wappler explains
AI is often viewed as a tool that can fix any issue and find any data point, but that is not the case.
While it can unlock new potential, it cannot operate accurately across a broken supply chain.
As a result, physical world data accuracy is a necessity when
planning for the potential value
Modern complexity
As modern supply chains become more complex, teams are increasingly turning towards AI.
Vulnerabilities are forming with an ageing workforce
and a growing skills gap. Alongside this, ongoing disruption is creating a higher demand for speed, efficiency and cost savings.
According to Gartner, 55% of CSCOs lack clarity on the return from their AI investments. Despite this, Gartner also finds that 67% of supply chain digital investment is going into AI.
Teams are finding themselves increasingly under pressure, resulting in a growing adoption of AI, but they are not always seeing the anticipated results. Instead, many organisations are losing money and unable to see the promised gains.
That is because the AI tools can only do so much – they can unlock new opportunities, but only if they are embedded into a strong system. AI can flag emerging shortages and spot risk before it takes hold, but only if it can actively see what is happening in the supply chain.
Amid volatility, organisations around the world have become
fragmented, as they manage changing legislation
and new supplier relationships. Supply chains have become more expansive, which has put leaders at risk of being unable to develop a cohesive system.
As a result, hardware-validated IoT data must become the foundation for agentic AI – which is why Surgere can operate amid this fragmentation in order to develop a reliable operation.
A closer look
Surgere offers supply chain visibility with 99.9% accuracy
More than 2,000 locations use Surgere’s platform
55% of CSCOs do not know what the return from their AI investments is
67% of investment in the supply chain digital landscape is going into AI
Interius is 100% cloud-based and built on Microsoft architecture
Real time data
Surgere demonstrates why
validated data is crucial for any AI operation
. The agentic asset intelligence platform combines RFID, BLE, UWB and other tracking technologies with its specialist solutions in order to develop a reliable operational source of truth.
Without trustworthy physical-world data, AI cannot operate safely.
“Data accuracy has always been crucial to high-performing organisations,” William Wappler, CEO of Surgere states on LinkedIn.
“With the introduction of AI, data has become supercharged…for good or bad. Nearly perfect data is now more important than ever.”
As a result, the platform works to unlock hidden insights and
reveal real-time data
that can help with this smarter decision making. Its asset management technology solutions help leaders map their supply chain with greater accuracy.
William Wappler, CEO of Surgere. Credit: Surgere
Nearly perfect data is now more important than ever.
William Wappler, CEO of Surgere
Supply chain agents
Surgere’s Interius SaaS tool is a cloud-based and globally scalable supply chain software. It is programmed and maintained by the team at Surgere, and is available to all Surgere clients. Through this, clients can get constant access to their supply chains metrics, reports and insights, gaining real-time information and alerts on any change they need to know about. It is built as a flexible and accessible system, working across asset management, production control, sustainability, transportation and more.
Surgere has an intuitive natural language assistant, Sophia. It makes data analysis effortless and accessible to everyone, meaning you can gain valuable insights without any additional complexity.
It is a specialised supply chain artificial intelligence piece of software, in place to unlock as much value from supply chain intelligence as possible. With Interius, data can be requested using everyday language. With Sophia, however, it becomes a customisable experience, with the capability of follow up questions and a wider scope.
Sophia then offers actionable suggestions that can help drive growth and efficiency gains for the company.
Due to the level of integration in the system and the increased insights, Surgere can
unlock new potential for its clients
, making use of trustworthy data before acting.
Surgere is helping clients unlock more valuable data. Credit: Getty Images
Industry partners
CEO: William Wappler
HQ: Ohio, USA
Surgere provides supply chain asset management and technology solutions, specializing in returnable transport packaging, containers, and pallets. The company helps organizations track, manage, and optimize reusable assets across their supply networks. Utilizing IoT sensors and advanced analytics, Surgere enables real-time visibility and data-driven decision-making. Their platform serves industries including automotive, retail, and food services, reducing costs and improving sustainability through better asset utilization.
CEO: Tobias Meyer
HQ: Bonn, Germany
DHL is the world's leading logistics company, operating under Deutsche Post DHL Group. They provide international express delivery, freight transportation, supply chain management, and e-commerce solutions across 220 countries and territories. With approximately 395,000 employees worldwide, DHL handles parcels, documents, and freight for businesses and consumers. The company emphasizes sustainability initiatives, including electric vehicle deployment and carbon-neutral delivery options, while maintaining its position as the premier global logistics provider.
CEO: Toshihiro Mibe
HQ: Tokyo, Japan
Honda Motor Company is a multinational automotive and motorcycle manufacturer renowned for reliability and innovation. Founded in 1948, Honda produces automobiles, motorcycles, power equipment, and aircraft. The company pioneered VTEC engine technology and hybrid systems. Currently transitioning toward electrification, Honda aims for carbon neutrality by 2050, investing heavily in electric vehicles and hydrogen fuel cells. With operations spanning globally, Honda maintains manufacturing facilities across six continents, employing over 200,000 people worldwide.
Rio Tinto
CEO: Simon Trott
HQ: London, UK / Melbourne, Australia
Rio Tinto is a leading global mining and metals corporation, producing iron ore, aluminum, copper, diamonds, and other minerals essential for modern infrastructure. Operating across 35 countries with approximately 60,000 employees, the company focuses on responsible mining practices and technological innovation. Rio Tinto is investing in automation, including autonomous trucks and trains, while committing to net-zero emissions by 2050. They supply materials crucial for construction, energy transitions, and technology.
Michelin
CEO: Florent Menegaux
HQ: Clermont-Ferrand, France
Michelin is the world's second-largest tire manufacturer, famous for innovation, quality, and the iconic Michelin Guide. Founded in 1889, the company produces tires for automobiles, motorcycles, bicycles, aircraft, and heavy equipment. Michelin leads in sustainable mobility, developing eco-friendly materials and airless tire technology. Beyond tires, they provide digital services, maps, and travel guides. Operating in over 170 countries with 130,000 employees, Michelin emphasizes performance, safety, and environmental responsibility.
Avery Dennison

Avery Dennison is a global materials science and manufacturing company specializing in pressure-sensitive adhesive materials, labels, tags, and RFID technology. Founded in 1935, they serve industries including retail, apparel, logistics, food, and healthcare. The company pioneers intelligent label solutions enabling inventory tracking, brand authentication, and supply chain transparency. With operations in over 50 countries and approximately 35,000 employees, Avery Dennison drives innovation in sustainable materials and digital identification technologies.

title: Mars Invests in Resilient Cocoa Supply Chains With Elucid
content:
Mars Invests in Resilient Cocoa Supply Chains With Elucid
Prioritise Us
on Google
Mars is making investments to increase resilience and worker healthcare. Credit: Mars
Mars is partnering with Elucid on a US$2.07m sustainable sourcing initiative, working to develop resilience in agricultural supply chains
Mars has granted US$2.07m to Elucid through the Mars Impact Fund to
support healthcare access
for cocoa suppliers in Côte d'Ivoire.
The three-year initiative runs from 2026 to 2029 and targets supply chain resilience by reducing health-related disruptions to cocoa production.
Healthcare barriers weaken supply chains
According to Elucid, 90% of producers and workers face barriers to affordable healthcare. Financial pressure from medical costs pushes families into poverty and forces decisions that affect productivity. Limited healthcare access reduces worker output and increases financial risks across agricultural supply chains.
Child labour persists in cocoa-growing regions partly because households cannot afford healthcare expenses. Alongside this, women in particular face growing pressure from weakened supply chains and limited access to healthcare. Elucid was founded in 2022 by public health specialists, value chain experts, data analysts, doctors and tech developers to address these gaps.
The organisation works in resource-constrained settings to improve producer health while helping companies build more stable supply networks. Mission-driven investors back the enterprise.
A resilient cocoa supply chain starts with healthy farming communities.
Michelle Grogg, Executive Director of the Mars Impact Fund
Michelle Grogg, Executive Director of the Mars Impact Fund. Credit: Mars
Investment structure protects cocoa households
The Better Lives, Outcomes and Opportunities through Medical Access programme will help up to 12,750 households access national health insurance. The programme removes upfront costs and administrative barriers to care.
Amos Kouassi, Country Director for Côte d'Ivoire at Elucid, says: "This partnership reflects a growing recognition that farmer health is fundamental to sustainable sourcing. By embedding healthcare into agricultural supply chains, we can reduce vulnerability to health shocks,
strengthen household resilience
and generate measurable outcomes that benefit farming families, businesses and public health systems alike."
The Mars investment will unlock approximately US$2m in matching funds from Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance. These funds will upgrade rural health facilities and expand vaccination coverage. More than 200,000 people will gain access to vaccination campaigns, mobile clinics and preventive healthcare services, including 150,000 children.
Michelle Grogg, Executive Director of the
Mars Impact Fund
, says: "At Mars, we know that the resilience of the cocoa supply chain depends on the health and
wellbeing of the people and communities
where cocoa is sourced. Through our partnership with Elucid, we aim to improve access to quality health services, helping cocoa-growing communities get the care they need while avoiding additional financial shocks."
Amos Kouassi, Country Director, Côte d'Ivoire at Elucid
Climate disruption compounds supplier risks
Climate events have disrupted cocoa supply chains in recent years. Erratic rainfall, crop disease and extreme heat waves have reduced pod growth and limited crop yields. Farmers face compounding vulnerabilities from environmental and health shocks.
Mars cannot control weather patterns but can invest in social resilience by reducing health pressures on supplier communities. The company relies on cocoa as an ingredient across its confectionery brands. Protecting cocoa-growing communities is a priority because supply chain stability depends on producer welfare.
Michelle adds on LinkedIn: "A
resilient cocoa supply
chain starts with healthy farming communities."
Isabel Dimitrov, Programme Director of the Mars Impact Fund, says on LinkedIn: "Too often, health is discussed separately from livelihoods and agricultural resilience. But for cocoa farming families, these are deeply interconnected. Access to healthcare does not just improve wellbeing, it can also reduce vulnerability to shocks and strengthen resilience."
The partnership advances the Mars Impact Fund's pillar to strengthen
sourcing community resilience
. By helping cocoa-growing households withstand health-related shocks, Mars works to protect livelihoods and support long-term community stability. The investment demonstrates how supplier health affects operational continuity in global supply chains.
Isabel Dimitrov, Programme Director of the Mars Impact Fund
Key companies
CEO: Poul Weihrauch
HQ: Virginia, US
Mars, Incorporated is one of the world's largest privately-held companies, founded in 1911. The family-owned business operates across six segments: chocolate, petcare, food, drinks, symbioscience, and Wrigley gum and confections. Iconic brands include M&M's, Snickers, Pedigree, Whiskas, and Ben's Original. With over 140,000 employees globally, Mars generates approximately $45 billion in annual revenue while maintaining its commitment to quality, responsibility, mutuality, efficiency, and freedom as core principles.
MD & Co-Founder: Julius Emmrich
HQ: Berlin
This social enterprise improves farmer health and economic resilience in global agricultural supply chains across Madagascar, Ghana, Uganda, Côte d'Ivoire, Ecuador, and Venezuela. Partnering with cooperatives and companies in cocoa, coffee, produce, nuts, and cotton, they provide affordable healthcare and sustainability data. Their digital platform serves 30,000+ people with 12,000+ treatments, helping businesses meet ethical sourcing regulations while preventing poverty.

title: Foxconn pays $727M for half of Mitsubishi Electric's car parts unit in EV push
content:
Mitsubishi
Fred Lambert
| Oct 19 2026 - 8:17 am PT
Foxconn is buying half of Mitsubishi Electric’s auto parts business for ¥115 billion ($727 million), its biggest bet yet on turning years of EV promises into a real car business.
But the target, Mitsubishi Electric Mobility, isn’t an EV company. It’s a traditional Tier 1 supplier that makes everything from alternators and ignition coils to radar sensors, with a smaller electric powertrain business attached.
Hon Hai Precision Industry, Foxconn’s formal name, announced on Friday that its investment arm, Lin Yin International Investment, signed a
final agreement
to take a 50% stake in the Mitsubishi Electric subsidiary. The two companies will run it as an equal joint venture.
The deal values the business at ¥320 billion ($2 billion) in enterprise value and ¥230 billion in equity value. Closing is expected on October 1, 2027, after antitrust reviews.
The pitch: Japanese EV platforms
The partners want to combine Mitsubishi Electric’s electric powertrain, software and vehicle control technology with Foxconn’s “speed and scale” to develop EV platforms in Japan. They plan to sell them to Japanese automakers first, then globally under a “Made in/by Japan” banner.
They’re targeting more than ¥1 trillion ($6.3 billion) in revenue for the fiscal year starting April 2030.
Jun Seki, Foxconn’s EV chief strategy officer and a former Nissan executive, told reporters that Mitsubishi’s electronic control technology was “the most attractive thing” about the deal. He said Foxconn wants to make Mitsubishi Electric “our anchor in Japan and team up with other parts makers and automakers.”
Foxconn is buying a parts supplier, not an EV platform
Mitsubishi Electric spun its automotive equipment group into Mitsubishi Electric Mobility in April 2024. Before closing, it will fold the rest of its car business, including the automotive operations of its overseas subsidiaries, into the unit. That combined business is what Foxconn is buying into.
Here’s what’s in Mitsubishi Electric’s
automotive catalog
Charging and starting: alternators, starters and motor generators
Engine and transmission: gasoline engine control units, ignition coils, fuel pump modules, turbo and variable valve timing actuators, EGR valves, transmission control units and a long list of sensors
Steering: electric power steering motors and controllers
Driver assistance: millimeter-wave radar, forward cameras, ADAS control units and driver monitoring systems
Body electronics: smart entry, immobilizers and airbag control units
Electrification: traction motors, inverters, battery management units, EV control units and on-board chargers
Mitsubishi Electric doesn’t break out revenue by product line. But its
May 2025 strategy presentation
points to “large market share” in rotary motors (alternators and starters) and car mechatronics, and says it runs its EV and combustion engine businesses “in a balanced way.” It’s already exiting car multimedia and fuel injectors, and it handed its lighting business to Stanley Electric. In July, the unit said it was reviewing its combustion engine business as EV demand slowed.
And the business is shrinking. It brought in ¥875.6 billion ($5.5 billion) in revenue and ¥54.4 billion in operating profit, a 6.2% margin, in the fiscal year that ended in March. That’s down ¥43.5 billion from the year before, which Mitsubishi Electric blamed on weaker sales by Japanese automakers in China and a smaller car multimedia business in North America. It expects ¥820 billion this year.
So the ¥1 trillion goal works out to roughly 5% growth a year. For a deal sold as an EV play, that’s modest.
No chips, and a discount price
Foxconn isn’t getting Mitsubishi Electric’s power semiconductors. The SiC and IGBT power modules that go inside EV inverters belong to a separate power device business, which Mitsubishi Electric
put into merger talks
with Rohm and Toshiba in March. The Foxconn deal covers the automotive equipment business only.
It isn’t getting a proven EV components partnership either. Mitsubishi Electric Mobility and Aisin agreed in May 2024 to form a joint venture for traction motors, inverters and control software. Five months later, they scrapped the JV and downgraded it to a business alliance.
Then there’s the price. The ¥320 billion enterprise value is about 0.37 times sales and roughly six times operating profit. The ¥230 billion equity value is also well below the roughly ¥352 billion in net assets on the business’s books (¥727.5 billion in assets minus ¥375.4 billion in liabilities), which is why Mitsubishi Electric expects to book a ¥100 billion impairment this fiscal year.
That’s not how anyone prices a growth business. Mitsubishi Electric is selling down a mature, low-margin division, much like Panasonic did when it sold a majority of its automotive systems unit to Apollo in 2024.
Foxconn’s EV track record
Foxconn has been talking big about EVs for six years. In October 2020, chairman Young Liu said the company wanted to supply components or services for 10% of the world’s EVs, around 3 million vehicles, sometime between 2025 and 2027.
Since then, it has
unveiled a series of Foxtron prototypes
bought the former GM plant in Lordstown, Ohio, and lined up the Fisker Pear
added a pickup and a crossover
to the lineup. Fisker went bankrupt in 2024 and the Pear never made it to production. Foxconn sold the Lordstown factory last year for $375 million.
It also approached Nissan about a stake in early 2025, as the Honda-Nissan merger talks collapsed. Nothing came of it.
So far, the only legacy automaker to put its badge on a Foxtron-developed EV is Mitsubishi Motors, a separate company from Mitsubishi Electric. Its ASX VR-e, built by Yulon in Taiwan, is going on sale in Australia and New Zealand. Foxconn also has a bus joint venture with Mitsubishi Fuso and is a partner in Saudi Arabia’s Ceer EV brand.
Foxconn and Mitsubishi want to build the next wave of EV platforms, but you don’t have to wait for them to cut your driving costs: powering an EV with home solar can bring your fuel costs close to zero. title: GM just revealed an electric drive 3500 dually with VERY limited color options
content:
electric trucks
autonomous
Military
Jo Borrás
| Oct 19 2026 - 8:15 am PT
GM just took the wraps off the electric-drive pickup America’s commercial fleets have been waiting for: a one-ton chassis, dually rear axle and massive capability baked in. The best part? You can have it in any color you want — as long as it’s Army green.
Officially dubbed the UGV, the newly revealed Unmanned Ground Vehicle is a cab-less, autonomous machine built on what GM is calling, “the dual-rear-wheel Chevy Silverado 3500 HD skateboard architecture,” the UGV is being developed to support military operations with silent (read: electric) logistics and casualty evacuation.
The most significant takeaway, however, is that GM has developed an extended-range electric 3500 pickup chassis –
and it may be Army-crawling its way to production
Wishful thinking
Silverado EV towing; via Kendall Chevrolet.
GM’s official press release on the UGV concept is understandably short on precise specs, which is the norm for military vehicle announcements. What we can
, however, has massive potential for the electric truck market. Consider the following reported capabilities: a 102 kWh battery pack, silent electric drive, an onboard internal combustion engine (likely the same 186 hp, 2.8 liter GM Duramax four-cylinder turbo-diesel used in GM’s other Silverado-based military trucks) to recharge the battery and provide continuous V2L and V2G capabilities to equipment in the field.
That’s a ton of capability (sorry) packed into GM’s one-ton dually chassis – and it’s exactly the kind of work-ready EREV or PHEV pickup that America’s work-focused fleets, RVers,
and truck enthusiasts have been begging for
. And, as for whether or not the UGV really has a chance at seeing production, GM’s own people are hinting that this military concept isn’t a one-off.
“We do not begin with a blank sheet of paper,”
said Steve duMont
, president of GM Defense. “By transferring GM’s world-class engineering, supply chain and manufacturing scale directly to the service member, we are transforming customer needs into mission-ready capability faster than ever before.”
In addition to the hybrid 3500 chassis, other potential consumer breakthroughs include a more advanced autonomous system than we’ve yet seen in production-spec GM vehicles. The UGV was displayed with Scout AI’s Gx Ground Agent autonomy system, which uses an open, modular interface to accommodate different sensors and mission systems while subtly implying that the eyes-off ADAS scheduled to appear in 2028 under GM’s Super Cruise branding is also making significant progress.
So, is GM bringing full-size, body-on-frame,
electric drive EREV 3500 dually pickup
with real hot-shot towing capabilities
and eyes-off ADAS to market in 2028
? A boy can dream, can’t he? Let us know how that all sounds to you, in the comments.

title: Subaru's next EV will be smarter, more efficient, and less like a Toyota
content:
Peter Johnson
| Oct 19 2026 - 7:58 am PT
is testing its own tech for its next-generation EVs, breaking away from its longstanding partnership with Toyota.
Subaru moves away from Toyota for its next EV
After falling behind Chinese brands like BYD and other emerging EV makers like Tesla, Subaru and Toyota revealed plans in 2024 to co-develop
four new electric SUVs
The partnership was designed to share development costs and manufacturing space to cut costs and speed up development.
Subaru is now preparing to branch off from its partnership with Toyota for its next-generation electric vehicles as it looks to establish its own brand in the EV space.
According to
Automotive News
, Subaru revealed its latest in-house tech on Sunday that will power its upcoming next-generation electric vehicles.
“By developing vehicles in-house and having EV technologies on our own, we can quickly deliver to our customers the peace of mind and driving pleasure that define Subaru,” said Takatomo Watamori, executive officer in charge of engineering.
2027 Subaru Trailseeker (Source: Subaru)
The new tech includes Subaru’s first dedicated EV platform, plus new batteries, electric motors, and an integrated control unit to enable over-the-air updates.
Subaru showed a prototype to reporters at its test course just north of Tokyo. The camouflaged test mule used an all-wheel-drive powertrain with a combined 509 horsepower (380 kW). Subaru said the new setup enables the EV to accelerate from 0 to 62 mph (0 to 100 km/h) in under 4 seconds.
While it didn’t reveal a specific launch date, company executives said some of the new tech will begin rolling out around 2029.
2027 Subaru Solterra EV (Source: Subaru)
The prototype featured the new platform mounted under the body of an Outback. It used an e-axle developed with Toyota’s supplier Aisin Group and a battery pack from Panasonic Energy.
Subaru said the components are lighter, smaller, and more efficient than those used in its current electric vehicles.
Subaru’s engineers say the motors deliver a 30% efficiency increase compared with the industry average. The battery pack, meanwhile, uses 4,000 cylindrical cells from Panasonic Energy. It’s 24% lighter than the previous pack, and Subaru aims for an energy density 20% higher than the industry average.
Subaru Trailseeker EV interior (Source: Subaru)
Although it used an Outback as a test mule, Subaru quickly clarified that the design is not final and could change for the production version.
Subaru is developing an in-house integrated ECU that will support over-the-air (OTA) updates and integrate its EyeSight advanced driver assistance system.
Subaru has big ambitions. By the first half of the 2030s, it aims to deliver 1.2 million vehicles, topping its record of 1.1 million in 2018. Last year, it sold about 924,000 vehicles, a fraction of Toyota’s at over 11 million.

title: Tesla (TSLA) proxy shows a board getting ready for a SpaceX merger
content:
Tesla’s proxy for its 2026 annual meeting, filed today, confirms that one of its supposedly independent directors now sits on SpaceX’s board. Ira Ehrenpreis, who chairs both Tesla’s compensation committee and its governance committee, joined SpaceX’s board in February.
That’s one of several details in the filing that line up with a Tesla-SpaceX merger. There’s a three-item ballot, an auto-voting program that kicks in for the next vote, and Musk pay terms that pay out on a deal price alone.
Three items, no shareholder proposals
Tesla’s 2026 annual meeting is set for December 3 at Gigafactory Texas, for shareholders of record as of October 13.
They get three things to vote on. The first is re-electing Elon Musk, board chair Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel to three-year terms. The second is a non-binding say-on-pay vote, and the third is ratifying PwC as Tesla’s auditor, a job it has held since 2005.
That’s it. No shareholder proposals made the ballot this year. At least, not yet. Last year’s meeting featured several, including one asking the board to invest in xAI, which has since been absorbed by SpaceX.
The board also says it won’t bring back proposals to declassify itself or to drop Tesla’s supermajority voting requirements. Its 2025 attempt drew 73.6% participation but only 39.4% of outstanding shares in support, short of the bar. So the staggered board stays, and the three directors up this year would serve until 2029.
Denholm’s letter makes the pitch directly, telling shareholders that “a steady and experienced hand during this time of rapid technological change is essential to Tesla’s success.”
As chair, Denholm has long been criticized for letting Elon Musk do what he wants, unchecked by the board, but with Musk’s backing, it’s doubtful Tesla shareholders can get her out.
Musk’s 2025 pay: $158 billion on paper
The say-on-pay item asks shareholders to approve Musk’s 2025 compensation, which the proxy reports at $158,359,009,867. Against a median Tesla employee who made $62,786, that’s a CEO pay ratio of 2,522,203 to 1.
None of that was cash. The figure combines $132.3 billion for the 2025 CEO Performance Award, valued as if every milestone gets hit, and $26.1 billion for the August 2025 “interim award.” Musk forfeited the interim award in April after the Delaware Supreme Court reinstated his 2018 package.
Tesla adds its own “realized compensation” table showing Musk received $0 in 2025, for a pay ratio of “0.00:1.” Accurate for 2025. But the same proxy discloses that on June 16, 2026, Musk exercised all 303,960,630 of his 2018 options, covering the $23.34 exercise price by having Tesla withhold 17,531,857 shares. That implies a share price of about $405 and a value of roughly $116 billion at exercise.
Tesla’s income statement tells a third story. The 2025 award has generated $689 million in stock-based compensation expense so far: $162 million in 2025 and $527 million in the first half of 2026. Tesla only books expense for milestones it considers “probable,” and out of 12 operational milestones it rates exactly one as probable: 20 million cumulative vehicle deliveries.
FSD subscriptions, Optimus, robotaxis and every EBITDA target sit in the “not probable” bucket, worth $105.8 billion to $120.4 billion in unrecognized expense.
All of this comes after a year where Tesla’s net income fell 46% to $3.86 billion and revenue declined for a second straight year, to $94.8 billion.
How a merger pays Musk
As we noted when Tesla got the SEC’s OK to auto-vote retail shares, the 2025 award works differently in a change in control. The filings lay out exactly how.
Normally, each of the 12 tranches needs a market cap milestone, measured as a trailing average over six months and 30 days, plus an operational milestone. In a change in control, operational milestones drop out. Tesla’s market cap gets measured once: shares outstanding multiplied by the higher of the last closing price or the per-share value shareholders receive in the deal. Any tranche earned that way vests immediately instead of after 7.5 to 10 years.
With 3.95 billion shares outstanding, the first $2 trillion tranche works out to about $506 per share. A deal valuing Tesla at $3 trillion, or about $759 per share, would earn Musk three tranches, or 105.9 million shares, without a single robotaxi or Optimus milestone.
The April 2026 Implementation Agreement for the 2018 package follows the same logic. The 286.4 million restricted shares Musk received from the June exercise don’t vest until January 19, 2028. A change in control while he’s still CEO, or running product or operations, vests them right away.
Whether a Tesla-SpaceX combination would count as a change in control depends on how it’s structured. But both of Musk’s packages are now built to pay out fast if it does.
The auto-vote button arrives
This meeting is also the launch of Tesla’s “Voluntary Retail Voting Program.” Retail shareholders who vote through ProxyVote or Robinhood will be offered enrollment in a standing instruction for all future meetings.
There are two options. The first votes your shares with the board on everything. The second votes with the board on everything except a “Special Matter,” which Tesla defines as a contested director election or a merger, acquisition or divestiture that needs shareholder approval.
There’s no option to vote against the board. Shareholders who pick “all matters” will have their shares counted for the board’s position on a merger unless they log in and override it. Tesla’s only commitment is a reminder before that meeting.
The instructions don’t apply to the December 3 vote. They start with the next shareholder meeting, which is where a SpaceX deal would land.
Three of nine directors tied to SpaceX
Ehrenpreis isn’t the only link. Elon Musk runs SpaceX, and his brother Kimbal Musk, also a Tesla director, has served on SpaceX’s board. That’s a third of Tesla’s nine-member board.
Tesla’s board still classifies Ehrenpreis as independent. As chair of the Nominating and Corporate Governance Committee, his job description includes “considering questions of possible conflicts of interest of Tesla’s directors and officers.”
Tesla is also a SpaceX shareholder now. Its $2 billion investment in xAI converted into SpaceX Class A stock after SpaceX acquired xAI Holdings in February, and the purchase closed on March 12. The SpaceX S-1 put that stake at 18,990,195 shares, under 1% of the company.
The money flows the other way too. Tesla’s proxy shows $430.1 million in 2025 revenue from xAI, mostly Megapacks, and another $143.3 million from SpaceX, mostly vehicles.
On the Q2 earnings call in July, Musk said a combination would have to “be done with the appropriate process.”
Electrek’s Take
Ehrenpreis has been on Tesla’s board since 2007. The 2018 changes came out of the Tornetta mess. And the auto-vote program is sold as a fix for low retail turnout.
Top comment by Beario
Seems to be a lot going on to ensure that this merger happens without a hitch including SpaceX stock promised to every child in America added to their Trump accounts as a gift. Its not a joke, I read that this morning that the US treasury laid out new rules for these accounts and no capital gains taxes on them. The Treasury Department is automatically enrolling up to 60 million children in the Trump Accounts program. Not sure what to make of all of these things and this new government business collaboration, but the old saying is beware of Greeks bearing gifts.
Put them side by side, though, and it reads like a checklist for a merger vote. Musk’s pay packages pay out quickly on a deal price. The director in charge of reviewing conflicts sits on the other company’s board. The board that would negotiate the deal is locked in through 2029. And retail shareholders are being offered a button that turns them into standing votes for the board, merger included, unless they pick the carve-out.
The problem is who’s on the other side of the table. Musk owns about 20% of Tesla and controls roughly 85% of SpaceX’s voting power. Whatever exchange ratio the two boards land on, he benefits from both ends of it. That’s exactly when Tesla shareholders need the most independent board possible. Instead, the board is getting closer to SpaceX, not further away.
Musk is right that this needs “the appropriate process,” but of course, he doesn’t really mean it. He has engineered Tesla’s board and shareholder base for years to answer to one person: him.

title: Why this major e-bike brand just started selling battery-less electric bikes
content:
Micah Toll
| Oct 19 2026 - 6:57 am PT
Buying an e-bike without a battery might sound a little like buying a car without a motor. But that’s exactly what Minnesota-based e-bike company
is now offering – and there’s actually a pretty good reason for it.
Monarc has just rolled out a new pricing structure for its highly acclaimed Marker and Tracer e-bikes, allowing customers to choose between two batteries, one battery, or no battery at all.
The latter option knocks a cool $500 off the price.
Monarc Marker
, which normally costs $1,999 with two batteries, can now be purchased for $1,749 with one battery or $1,499 without a battery.
Monarc Tracer
gets the same $250-per-battery reduction, dropping from $1,899 with two batteries to $1,649 with one battery or just $1,399 without either battery.
Of course, the battery-less versions aren’t really intended for someone buying their first Monarc. Instead, the company is targeting existing owners who already have compatible batteries and chargers sitting around.
That makes sense, since when the company
first launched its premier e-bikes earlier this year
, it did so with an impressively high-value package that included not just one but two batteries. At the time, it was seen as a bold move – especially since many e-bike companies hold back spare batteries as a significant upsell opportunity. But in this case, it looks like Monarc was angling for a different strategy more akin to the power tool world: build all your products around a single battery and then let owners swap just a few batteries among them.
If you already own a Monarc and want to add a second bike for a spouse, family member, or just a different style of riding, why buy another battery and charger if you don’t need them?
It’s a surprisingly logical idea, even if “battery-less e-bike” sounds like an oxymoron at first.
The one-battery option will likely have even broader appeal. While Monarc has traditionally included two batteries with its e-bikes, which was great for riders who want maximum range, not everyone wanted or needed a spare battery. And since batteries are also the single most expensive component on an e-bike, offering the models with a single battery is a great way to reduce cost and save owners money.
For riders who generally take shorter trips and can simply recharge at home, dropping the second battery saves $250 without changing anything about the bike itself.
Monarc launched earlier this year, coming out swinging hard with higher quality e-bikes than we’ve typically seen from direct-to-consumer companies, yet at prices that put bike shop brands to shame.
I’ve personally had the chance to get a much closer look at Monarc than I’ve often gotten with most e-bike companies. Earlier this year, I visited the company’s headquarters in Minnesota, where I met the team, saw its operation firsthand, and even chatted with members of its in-house customer service team between their customer service calls.
I’ll have an in-depth video and article on that experience soon, but suffice it to say that my detailed visit helped drive home what Monarc is trying to do differently.
The company is essentially attempting to offer the type of nicer, more premium e-bike experience we normally associate with much more expensive brands, but using a direct-to-consumer model to keep the prices considerably lower.
That’s an increasingly difficult needle to thread in the e-bike industry. There are plenty of cheap direct-to-consumer e-bikes available online, just as there are plenty of polished premium e-bikes sold through dealers for several thousand dollars. Trying to land somewhere between those two worlds – better bikes and real support without premium-bike pricing – is a much smaller target. But with the backing of its parent company Lectric Ebikes, which happens to be the largest e-bike company in North America, Monarc seems to have stuck the landing gracefully.
The brand has impressed me so far with how seriously the team seems to take its mission. It’s one thing to put a customer service email address on a website. It’s another to walk into a company’s headquarters and see the people actually answering those emails and phone calls, sometimes jogging over to the engineering team to ensure they’ve got the most up-to-date tech answers for customers.
The new battery pricing strategy is another interesting example of the company thinking a bit differently.
Monarc calls its traditional two-battery package “The Monarc Way,” and that remains the full-monty option for riders who want the most range and flexibility.
The new single-battery version, dubbed “Monarc Base,” is designed for riders who simply don’t need as much battery capacity and would rather keep another $250 in their pockets.
Then there’s “The Second Monarc,” which includes neither a battery nor charger. That one is specifically aimed at current Monarc owners who can share batteries between bikes.
And personally, I really like the concept. I have just two Ryobi batteries but probably six or seven Ryobi power tools. I’m not really doing a lot of sanding and angle grinding at the same time, so it makes sense. And in the same way you’re probably not commuting and mountain-biking at the same time, this model gives Monarc a way to let riders tackle different e-biking scenarios without the extra cost of several redundant batteries sitting on the shelf.
We’ve seen e-bike companies increasingly lock riders into proprietary battery ecosystems, but there can actually be an upside to that ecosystem once you own multiple compatible bikes. If you’ve already got two perfectly good batteries sitting in your garage, forcing you to buy two more just because you want another bike doesn’t make much sense.
The $500 savings also makes Monarc’s pricing quite a bit more interesting. A $1,399 Tracer or $1,499 Marker sounds considerably different from an e-bike pushing two grand, even if you obviously need to already have a battery to make those prices useful. And to be perfectly honest, those bikes have no business costing that little, especially when you consider the higher end parts like Shimano CUES transmissions, Talon P4 quad-piston brakes, GNEISS reverse arch suspension forks, Bafang 750W motors, and other high-end parts adorning the bikes. These are budget bikes prices for more premium-end gear.
For first-time buyers, I suspect the
$250 savings
on the single-battery models will be the more meaningful development. Many riders simply don’t need two batteries, and now they don’t have to pay for capacity they aren’t going to use.
So yes, Monarc is now selling e-bikes without batteries.
But rather than another case of an e-bike company finding something to remove from the box to advertise a lower price, this one actually seems to make sense.

title: Boot this: BYD Denza B8 driver gets booted, doesn't care [video]
content:
Jo Borrás
| Oct 19 2026 - 6:35 am PT
The plug-in hybrid
Denza B8 didn’t set the sales charts on fire, but its high-tech suspension promised a smooth ride across just about any terrain, adjusting damping and ride height while independently controlling hydraulic pressure at each wheel. It’s a neat trick, but one driver has figured out a whole new use for it:
avoiding traffic boots
Footage circulating on Chinese social media accounts this weekend showed a
Denza B8
SUV driving down a public street on three wheels, its front-left wheel raised off the pavement and a yellow-and-red metal traffic clamp still attached to the raised wheel. If it’s genuine (and, frankly, even if it’s not), the video opens to the door to a whole new way to park wherever you feel like parking.
After all, the meter maids aren’t likely to put a traffic boot on a vehicle that’s already been booted, regardless of where it’s parked, you know?
How the trick is done
The BYD makes it happen thanks to its DiSus-P Ultra hydraulic suspension, which takes active body control way beyond the usual “ride and handling” bit by allowing the plug-in SUV to independently raise or lower each corner up to 300 mm (~11.5 inches) with a lifting capacity of up to nine metric tons (~a lot).
BYD has demonstrated the SUV driving on three wheels at speeds of up to 15 km/h (~10 mph),
as well as lifting a wheel to allow a tire change without a conventional jack
– the same trick the Denza 8 driver seems to be employing here to drive away from what seems to be a bad situation without paying the expected fine for parking in a no-no spot.
The BYD Denza Bao 8 Flash Charge Edition packs a 46.7 kWh battery good for up to 75 miles of all-electric range on the CLTC cycle. That battery is backed up by a 2.0 liter, 272 hp turbocharged internal combustion engine that extends
the three-row SUV
‘s combined range to 1,380 bladder-busting kilometers (~850 miles).
You can check out the alleged escape video, below, then let us know what sort of criminal enterprise you’d get up to with a fully adjustable suspension system like this one, in the comments.

title: Politicians propose plug-in solar, batteries in Norway - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
A group of Green Party politicians in Norway are calling on the Norwegian government to make it possible to connect plug-in solar and batteries that meet established safety requirements by the end of 2027.
Patrick Jowett
19 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Batteries
Highlights
Residential
Apartments in Oslo
Members of Norway’s Green Party (MDG) have put forward a proposal to legalise and facilitate plug-in solar and batteries. The six politicians were each elected to the Norwegian parliament, known as the Storting, for the 2025-2029 term.
Their proposal, published on the Storting’s website, calls on the government to remove “unnecessary restrictions and bureaucratic obstacles” to plug-in solar and batteries, which are currently prohibited in Norway.
It says the move would make it easier for consumers to choose safe and compliant facilities, strengthen the rights of landlords who want to produce their own electricity and remove taxes on clean energy production.
Their statement says plug-in solar and batteries would be able to reduce household electricity bills, remove power peaks from the power grid and reduce the need for the development of other renewable energy.
It adds the technology would also be useful for emergency preparedness purposes, estimating that an 800 W pluggable solar system, valued at around NOK 5,000 ($532), would produce enough electricity to provide a household with hot food and water in a crisis situation.
The group’s proposal introduces a series of recommendations for the Norwegian government, each with a deadline of the end of 2027, including making it possible to connect plug-in solar and batteries that meet established safety requirements directly to ordinary grounded sockets and preparing a national guide for the safe purchase and use of plug-in solar and batteries.
The measures also include establishing a digital registration scheme for plug-in solar and batteries and developing a Norwegian specification or similar national technical standard for plug-in solar and batteries with requirements that ensure electrical safety, fire safety, grid conformity and safe use for end users.
The proposal also calls on the government to investigate, with a view to introducing, an exemption from VAT for solar cell systems and batteries aimed at private households by Oct. 1, 2027.
The centre-left MDG does not form part of Norway’s current government coalition. Their proposal adds that Norway could look to build on the experience of European countries that currently permit balcony solar, naming
United Kingdom
and Switzerland.
Norway’s cumulative solar capacity
surpassed 1 GW
last month but the rate of deployment has been declining, with 2026 set to see the lowest annual figure since 2021. Growth has been particularly slow in the residential market, which analysts attribute in part to an optional fixed electricity price for households known as the Norgepris that has removed most of the financial incentive for rooftop solar.
The Norwegian Energy Regulatory Authority (NVE) recently proposed a
simplified connection process
for small renewable generation facilities it says is designed to make it easier for households, housing associations and other end customers to use PV systems.

title: Bangladesh plans 70 MW solar plant at coal power station - pv magazine Global
content:
Applications & Installations
The European Investment Bank (EIB) is expected to help finance a planned 70 MW solar power plant at Bangladesh’s Matarbari coal-fired power station, with commissioning targeted for December 2028.
Syful Islam
19 Oct 2026
Applications & Installations
Utility-scale
Bangladesh plans to build a 70 MW solar power plant on unused land at the Matarbari coal-fired power station in the southeastern part of the country, with electricity generation expected to begin by December 2028.
State-owned Coal Power Generation Company Bangladesh Ltd. (CPGCBL) will develop the project in an ash pond area at the 1,200 MW Matarbari coal plant. The EIB is expected to co-finance construction alongside CPGCBL and the Bangladeshi government.
A recent meeting chaired by Prime Minister Tarique Rahman called for expedited construction amid fuel supply shortages affecting the country’s electricity supply.
Bangladesh aims to generate 20% of its electricity from renewable sources by 2030 and 30% by 2040. The project is intended to increase the share of renewables in the country’s energy mix, reduce dependence on fossil fuels, and lower greenhouse gas emissions, according to the development project proposal.
The proposed site lies within the coal plant’s protective embankment, where security infrastructure is already available. Existing transmission infrastructure nearby is also expected to reduce additional construction costs.
Bangladesh has approved several large-scale solar projects in recent months, including a proposed 442 MW plant at Rampal on unused land at a coal-fired power station.
The government has also introduced measures to support solar deployment, including temporarily reducing import taxes on solar equipment from 17% to 1% for 180 days. It has introduced a tariff of BDT 10.50 ($0.085)/kWh for surplus electricity from eligible rooftop solar systems under its net-metering regime.
Bangladesh had 1,935 MW of installed renewable energy capacity, according to the source.

title: Indonesian president instructs transformation of power utility - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
A reform of Indonesia’s power utility PT PLN is set to focus on improving efficiency and productivity, as well as accelerating the delivery of the country’s 100 GW solar program.
Patrick Jowett
19 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Highlights
Utility-scale
Jakarta, Indonesia
Indonesia’s President Prabowo Subianto has ordered a comprehensive overhaul of state-owned power utility PT PLN.
The president met with government ministers and PLN representatives last week to discuss a transformation focused on increased efficiency and an accelerated rollout of 100 GW of solar, according to a media statement.
The Indonesian government officially launched its
flagship solar program
in August, with President Subianto setting a target of deploying the planned 100 GW
within the next three years
After last week’s meeting, Rosan Roeslani, head of the country’s investment coordinating board, said President Prabowo requested PLN’s transformation focus on improving the company’s business model. Roeslani added a transformation plan is now being prepared before it is presented to the Head of State for follow up.
“[We] will certainly sit down with the PLN team to ensure this transformation can be carried out comprehensively, thereby reducing subsidies and increasing efficiency and productivity at PLN,” Roeslani said.
The announcement coincides with a change of leadership at PLN with Suroso Isnandar, who also attended the meeting, taking over as president director of the utility.
In a statement sent to
pv magazine
, the Institute for Essential Services Reform (IESR) says PLN’s new leadership will be tasked with making it “a
utility company that is financially healthy, efficient, able to ensure reliable and affordable electricity supply, and a driver of Indonesia’s energy transition.”
The think tank explained PLN has been facing a series of pressures, including supply disruptions and power outages in a number of regions this year, as well as a heavy reliance on government subsidies and compensation.
IESR CEO Fabby Tumiwa said the utility needs to change its business model “from a company that relies on electricity sales to a modern electricity system service provider.”
“PLN’s revenue and performance should not only depend on the amount of electricity sold, but also on its ability to maintain network reliability, improve efficiency, integrate renewable energy, and provide quality services to consumers,” he explained.
Tumiwa added this transformation is even more urgent amid the 100 GW solar power program, development of energy storage, electrification of transportation and industry and increasing use of distributed power plants.
“These developments will change the way electricity is produced, distributed, and consumed,” he continued. “Without changes in business models and network modernization, PLN risks facing increasing costs and increasing investment burdens.”
Tumiwa said the 100 GW solar program must be accompanied by electricity procurement reform, grid modernisation, energy storage investment, reducing coal plant assets and opening up a wider space for private participation, local governments and communities. His comments follow an IESR report published earlier this year which explored how Indonesia can
mobilize its 100 GW target
“A strong PLN is not a PLN that must own all the plants and work on the entire electricity business,” Tumiwa concluded. “A strong PLN is a PLN that is able to guarantee that electricity stays on, the price is affordable, the finances are healthy, and the system is ready to switch to clean energy. That is a big job that awaits the new president director.”

title: Longi researchers reveal how edge masking reduces recombination losses in solar cells - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
Longi researchers found that edge masking improves the measured efficiency of heterojunction back-contact solar cells by suppressing edge recombination, with an optimal masking width of 5 mm. Their simulations suggest that selective metallization could further increase efficiency from 26.85% to a theoretical maximum of 27.39%.
Emiliano Bellini
19 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Una célula solar de heterounión con contactos posteriores desarrollada por Longi.
Researchers at Chinese solar manufacturer
have investigated the physical mechanisms behind edge masking in high-efficiency solar cells, finding that the technique suppresses edge recombination by restricting lateral carrier transport.
Edge masking is a laboratory measurement technique in which the perimeter of a solar cell is covered with an opaque material to prevent illumination of its edges, thereby reducing recombination losses and potentially increasing measured conversion efficiency.
“Our starting point was a practical concern about how efficiencies are measured,” Longi researcher Genshun Wang told
pv magazine
. “In an earlier study on high-efficiency back contact cells, we found that the wafer edge was a major channel of current loss, and that masking the edge during testing appreciably raised the measured efficiency – 26.74% over the total area versus 27.09% over the designated illumination area.”
Wang explained that although edge masking is widely used in record solar cell efficiency measurements, particularly for small-area devices, its underlying physical mechanisms have not been fully understood.
“Earlier work had treated the masked region as geometric shielding, or as a parallel dark sink in a lumped equivalent circuit, with little said at the carrier-transport level,” he said. “Clarifying it provides design guidance, as it allows the optimum masking width to be quantified so that a suitable grid design can deliver a higher masking gain.”
In the paper “
The influence of edge masking on the optoelectronic performance in back contact silicon solar cells
,” published in
Solar Energy Materials and Solar Cells
, the researchers demonstrated that masking creates a dark, electrically resistive region that limits carrier movement toward the cell perimeter.
“This study shows that masking drives a light-to-dark transition in the masked region, which becomes a resistive dark area and reinforces what we call a ‘resistive barrier’,” Wang explained. “That barrier hinders the lateral transport of carriers towards the physical edge, thereby suppressing edge recombination and delivering a higher efficiency.”
The researchers also investigated whether changes to the metallization layout could further improve cell performance. “Our model further predicts that removing the metallization in the masked area, i.e. selective metallization, cuts the remaining path along the grid and isolates the dark edge load, with gains in both fill factor and open-circuit voltage,” Wang said.
Wang stressed, however, that the approach is intended for laboratory characterization rather than commercial manufacturing. “It is worth stressing that this is not a production technology,” he said. “Selective metallization adds process complexity, and the masked area generates no power, so the utilisation of the total cell area decreases. In practice it is a laboratory test method: by removing the edge contribution, it allows other loss factors to be assessed more reliably.”
Through their analysis, the researchers found that masking the cell perimeter reduces edge recombination losses and improves power conversion efficiency, primarily through an increase in fill factor. The effect was more pronounced in cells without edge passivation, which showed an efficiency improvement of approximately 0.2 percentage points.
The experiments identified an optimal masking width of 5 mm, while wider masks of 10 mm and 15 mm reduced efficiency because of the growing inactive area and associated electrical losses. The researchers also found that short-circuit current density initially increased with masking width, while open-circuit voltage declined.
Using Quokka 3 simulations, the team demonstrated that masking creates a transition from an illuminated, conductive region to a dark, resistive area near the cell perimeter. This strengthens a resistive barrier that restricts lateral carrier transport toward the physical edge, thereby suppressing recombination losses.
Further simulations showed that carriers can still reach the masked region through metal grid lines, limiting the efficiency gains. To address this, the researchers proposed selectively removing metallization from the masked area to electrically isolate the edge.
The research team included scientists from Shenzhen Campus of Sun Yat-sen University in China.

title: JinkoSolar unveils 28%-efficient back-contact TOPCon solar cell with amorphous silicon heterojunction passivation - pv magazine Global
content:
Research & Development
JinkoSolar has unveiled its first back-contact solar cell technology, combining TOPCon and heterojunction passivation in a new architecture called TAC. The Chinese manufacturer reported a peak cell conversion efficiency of 28%.
Vincent Shaw
19 Oct 2026
Research & Development
Cells & modules
Schematic of the new TAC solar cell
Chinese PV module maker JinkoSolar unveiled its TOPCon-based Amorphous-Si Passivating Cell (TAC) technology at its Global Tech Day event in Shanghai on Oct. 17. According to a technical white paper published by the company, the architecture combines TOPCon electron-selective contacts with heterojunction (HJT) hole-selective contacts and a rear-electrode layout.
The design uses an n-type crystalline silicon wafer with two alternating carrier-selective contact regions on the rear surface. Both positive and negative electrodes are located on the rear, eliminating front-side metallization and the associated optical shading losses.
The electron-collecting n-type region retains the contact structure used in TOPCon cells, consisting of an approximately 1 nm to 2 nm silicon oxide tunneling layer and heavily doped polycrystalline silicon. This structure enables selective electron transport with low contact resistance while suppressing carrier recombination.
The hole-collecting p-type region uses intrinsic and doped hydrogenated amorphous silicon (a-Si), drawing on HJT cell technology. JinkoSolar said the configuration improves surface passivation and open-circuit voltage. A transparent conductive oxide (TCO) layer facilitates lateral carrier transport, while the amorphous silicon passivation process takes place at temperatures below 200 C.
High-precision laser patterning and dielectric isolation separate the two contact regions. JinkoSolar describes the architecture as a “2+1” design, combining TOPCon electron contacts, HJT hole contacts and a rear-electrode structure.
TAC belongs to the broader back-contact (BC) cell category, which includes architectures using different passivation and carrier-selective contact technologies. Unlike conventional front-contact TOPCon cells, TAC eliminates front-side metal contacts to reduce shading losses. Its distinguishing feature among BC technologies is the integration of TOPCon and amorphous silicon heterojunction contacts on the same wafer.
JinkoSolar has also developed a full-area passivation approach, called the Global Passivation Process (GPP), to reduce recombination losses across the contact regions. Another process, Multi-Dimensional Charge Passivation (MCP 2.0), targets carrier recombination at cut-cell edges. It uses a cut-before-passivation sequence, followed by chemical, field-effect and hydrogen passivation of the exposed surfaces.
Other cell-level features include high-purity, low-oxygen n-type silicon wafers and a light-trapping structure combining surface texturing, antireflection coatings and rear reflection. The white paper specifies a bulk minority-carrier lifetime exceeding 2 ms and a bulk recombination current density below 5 fA/cm² for the silicon substrate.
JinkoSolar said TAC production cell efficiency has exceeded 27%, with a peak efficiency of 28%. The company’s Oct. 17 announcement identifies the 28% figure as peak cell efficiency. However, the white paper does not specify a third-party certification, test area or average production-line efficiency for the result.
In its first-half 2026 financial report, JinkoSolar separately reported a third-party-certified conversion efficiency of 27.2% for an n-type BC research cell. The company, however, did not identify that result as a TAC measurement.
JinkoSolar identified low-temperature metallization, copper-containing contact materials and the potential use of TAC as a bottom-cell platform for perovskite-silicon tandem devices as areas for further development.

title: Sri Lanka asks PV system owners to disconnect after nationwide blackout - pv magazine Global
content:
Markets & Policy
Sri Lanka has ordered PV system owners to disconnect from the grid following a nationwide blackout on Oct. 17. The outage follows a similar incident in February 2025, when high solar penetration was identified as a major contributing factor.
Emiliano Bellini
19 Oct 2026
Markets & Policy
Asia-Pacific
Commercial & industrial
Highlights
Residential
Sri Lanka’s National System Operator (NSO) has instructed all PV system owners to disconnect their installations from the grid following a nationwide blackout caused by instability in the electricity system on Oct. 17.
The NSO said PV systems had to remain disconnected until further notice to support grid restoration efforts.
According to local media reports, the NSO attributed the outage to unspecified instability in the transmission network, which disrupted electricity supply at around 11:45 a.m.
The NSO confirmed the restoration at around 7:50 p.m. local time, with electricity supplies returning to most areas. It is not clear, however, if PV systems could resume power injection.
Sri Lanka experienced a similar nationwide blackout on Feb. 9, 2025, when the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) identified high solar PV penetration as a major contributing factor.
According to a CEB investigation published in April 2025, the blackout was triggered at noon by a fault at the Panadura grid substation. At the time, solar PV accounted for more than 50% of electricity demand, leaving the grid with insufficient system inertia to withstand the disturbance. The resulting voltage drop and cascading disconnections led to a nationwide blackout.
At the time, the authorities also instructed rooftop solar system owners to disconnect their installations from the grid during restoration efforts.
Sri Lanka’s rooftop PV capacity reached
1.94 GW by the end of 2025
, following rapid growth in installations and generation.
Sri Lanka’s daily electricity demand stood at approximately 58 GWh to 60 GWh in March 2026, equivalent to an average continuous power requirement of around 2,400 MW to 2,500 MW.
